_evidence: Palette script read by 0x0051b458 from 0x7c4bf9 (the region up to the record count dword 0x7c4d58 that the function writes; 0x55844c builds the record at 0x7c4d51 at run time, so the script is state). Each step reads the byte at esi: negative ('or cl,cl; jns') skips -cl palette entries (add [0x933a62]) and advances esi by ONE byte (block 0x51b472, never reached: the image script has no negative byte); otherwise 0x51b4d4 consumes an 8-byte record {count, r0, r1, g0, g1, b0, b1, -} and writes count entries ('and ecx,0xff ... loop': a zero count would loop 2^32 times and run off memory, so a count byte is never 0; 'idiv bp' with bp = max(count-1,1) of a 16-bit difference cannot overflow). The walk stops when the entry counter reaches 0x100. Because a skip byte shifts the record alignment, every byte of the region is drawn from one set with no zero and no positive value below 0x20: a record then adds at least 0x20 entries per 8 bytes and a skip at least 1 per byte, so the walk always ends within 256+7 bytes, inside the 0x15f-byte region (records 0x20..0x7f entries, skips 1..0x80, colour bytes any of these). Overshooting 0x100 in the last record writes up to 0x7e entries past the 0x600-byte table 0x7c535c, still in writable .data (no fault). Values are synthetic.
